speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: how long have you been experiencing this weakness and fatigue? Also, have you noticed any other symptoms like fever, weight loss, or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of outdoor activities and recent illnesses is concerning for an infectious or autoimmune etiology. Have you noticed any specific muscle weakness that makes lifting objects or climbing stairs difficult, and do you have any skin rashes or changes in your saliva or tears?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of weakness worsening later in the day and new-onset mild diplopia (double vision) is highly suggestive of this autoimmune neuromuscular disorder. I would like to confirm this with an Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test and request images of the extraocular muscles if available.
